name: Bug triage
description: Parse before searching, find known duplicates, triage with the rubric.

parts.text:
Our checkout is throwing this:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/svc/api/routes.py", line 88, in checkout
    totals = compute_totals(cart)
  File "/app/svc/pricing/aggregate.py", line 142, in compute_totals
    return sum(float(item["price"]) for item in items)
ValueError: could not convert string to float: 'N/A'

This is already known. Ticket 1 covers the same failure: checkout returns 500 on large orders, with the root cause in svc/pricing/aggregate.py line 142 in compute_totals, where a non-numeric price reaches float(). It is P1 - High, In Progress, assigned to maya.okafor@example.com. The trigger is a price of 'N/A' in the cart data rather than the item count itself.
Customers say they can't buy anything when their basket has a couple of dozen products. Should I file a bug?

No new ticket needed - this is already tracked twice. Ticket 1 is the engineering ticket (P1 - High, In Progress, maya.okafor@example.com) and ticket 8 is the customer-reported version of the same problem. Worth merging 8 into 1 rather than opening a third.
Getting ConnectionResetError from site-packages/vendorpay/transport.py. Is this us?

The failing frame is in the vendor library, not our code, so this is not a bug in our service. Ticket 2 already tracks it (P2 - Medium, Open), and the vendor-pay 3.5.0 changelog describes a keep-alive fix that matches these symptoms. Upgrading the SDK is the likely resolution.
Production API is returning 500s for every user and there's no workaround. How bad is this?
P0 - Critical. The rubric scores this at 90: production is down or unusable (50), all users are affected (20), and no workaround exists (20). That clears the 70-point P0 threshold.
The export is broken. What priority?

I need the impact before I can give you a defensible priority. Is production affected, how many users, is there a workaround, and is any data lost? Guessing at those would produce a confident number with nothing behind it.
